html:
Christ the Redeemer is a huge statue of Jesus with open arms on top of Corcovado mountain, above Rio de Janeiro in Brazil. It was built between 1922 and 1931.

The Brazilian engineer Heitor da Silva Costa designed it, and the French sculptor Paul Landowski shaped the figure. It is made of reinforced concrete covered in small triangles of soapstone. The statue is about 30 metres tall, standing on an 8 metre pedestal, and its arms stretch about 28 metres.

The idea came from Catholic groups in Rio after Brazil became a republic and separated church and state. Money was raised from the faithful across the country. Its clean, simple lines make it one of the best known works of Art Deco.

It quickly became the symbol of Rio and of Brazil itself. In 2007 it was voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. Lightning strikes it several times a year, and its fingers and head have been repaired more than once.
sum: Christ the Redeemer is a huge statue of Jesus with open arms on top of Corcovado mountain, above Rio de Janeiro in Brazil. It was built between 1922 and 1931.
